summary: Critical-fix frontend retest completed across 1920x800, 1440x900, 1024x768, 768x1024, 390x844, and 320x700. Previously blank Work/Proof/Gallery physical media now render with authentic images and red/white palette is largely correct; one remaining readability bug found in desktop hero title at required settled checkpoint.

ui_bugs.issue: At home 0.42 on desktop (1920x800 and 1440x900), hero title lines are vertically clipped (not fully readable) despite waiting >2s after transition, violating settled-readability requirement.

issues: Typography mask/layout causes partial clipping of hero words in settled frame.

action_items: Fix hero title clipping at settled desktop checkpoints (home 0.42) so all hero lines are fully readable at 1920x800 and 1440x900.
Re-run only hero settled screenshots after fix to confirm readability without mid-animation masking artifacts.
critical_code_review_comments: No new critical rendering-code defect found for previously blocked media planes; channel faces, credential face, and gallery photo planes are now visible on physical surfaces.
No /api calls, no 404 resources, and no server-side errors observed during regression runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Critical visual blocker from iteration_1 is resolved: in-scene channel/ID/gallery media are now visible on all tested viewports and laptop screen/keyboard are visible. Remaining issue is hero text clipping at settled desktop checkpoints. Controls smoke passed (anchors, enter, explore, mobile menu escape/tab smoke, ID modal escape, photo prev/next/modal, motion toggle, OS reduced-motion preference reaction, exact contact links).
rca of the issue: Desktop hero clipping appears to be a typography/animation layout issue: hero line wrappers (`.line` overflow hidden with large desktop font sizes) still clip text at 1920x800/1440x900 settled frame, likely due final y-position/line box composition rather than WebGL scene failure.
